blocks.headline: Die Wochentage
blocks.bodyEnglish:
The German week starts on Monday.
Every weekday is a noun with der, and you say am + day.

blocks.headline: Gehen wir ins Kino?
blocks.bodyEnglish: Sophie invites Betty to the cinema. Saturday does not work. Wednesday works.

turns.speaker: Sophie
turns.english: Shall we go to the cinema?

blocks.title: Gut gesagt: Nein!
blocks.bodyEnglish:
Germans often avoid a hard »nein«.
Casual speakers say »nee« or »nö«.
In Bavaria and Austria you hear »na«.
Polite standard: »Das geht leider nicht.«
blocks.bodyGerman:
Nee, das geht leider nicht.
Nein, das geht leider nicht.

blocks.headline: Die Ja-/Nein-Frage
blocks.bodyEnglish:
A yes/no question has no question word.
The verb moves to position 1 and the person follows it.

blocks.explanationEnglish:
A yes/no question has no question word. You ask with a rising voice.
Take the statement and move the conjugated verb to position 1.
Wir gehen ins Kino. → Gehen wir ins Kino?
The ending stays with the verb: Kochst du gern? — Kochen Sie gern?
Trap: ✗ Wir gehen ins Kino? → ✓ Gehen wir ins Kino?
blocks.englishBridge: English needs do: Do we go? German has no do — the verb alone leads the question.
blocks.targetSentenceEnglish: Shall we go to the cinema?

examples.english: Do we go to the cinema?

blocks.explanationEnglish:
A W-question starts with a question word: was, wann, wo, wer.
Then comes the conjugated verb, then the person: Wann gehen wir?
The answer gives the information the W-word asks for: Am Montag.
English keeps the person first: When we go. German moves the verb up.
Trap: ✗ Wann wir gehen? → ✓ Wann gehen wir?
blocks.englishBridge: English helps with do: When do we go? German needs no do — the W-word and the verb lead.
blocks.targetSentenceEnglish: When shall we go to the cinema?

examples.english: What do you like to do?

blocks.title: Sich verabreden
blocks.explanationEnglish: First you propose an activity. Then you fix a day. The partner answers with Ja or Nein.

examples.german: Gehen wir am Freitag ins Kino?
examples.english: Shall we go to the cinema on Friday?

items.english: Shall we go to the cinema?

blocks.explanationEnglish: A yes/no question starts with the conjugated verb: Gehen + wir + ins Kino?

items.sentence: Der erste Tag der Woche ist der ___.

blocks.explanationEnglish: The German week starts on Monday. Wednesday sits in the middle of the week, so it is called Mittwoch.

blocks.prompt: Build the question: »Gehen wir am Freitag ins Kino?«
blocks.explanationEnglish: The verb is already first. Next comes the subject wir, then the day and the place.
